lessons.title: So + adjective/adverb + that + result
lessons.content: 'So … that' is used to show cause and effect. The structure is 'so + adjective or adverb + that + result clause'. It connects a quality (cause) with its consequence (result).

details.explanation: Use 'so' before an adjective to show the degree of something causes a result.
details.example: The water is so salty that I cannot drink it.
details.burmese: ရေက အရမ်းငန်လို့ ငါမသောက်နိုင်ဘူး။

details.explanation: Use 'so' before an adverb to show how an action causes a result.
details.example: We arrived so late that we could not have dinner.

lessons.title: Combining sentences with So … that
lessons.content: Two simple sentences can be combined into one using 'so … that'. The first sentence provides the cause (quality) and the second provides the result. Pattern: Subject + is/verb + so + adjective/adverb + that + result clause.

details.explanation: 'The box is very heavy' (cause) + 'I cannot lift it' (effect) become one sentence with 'so … that'.
details.example: The box is so heavy that I cannot lift it.
details.burmese: กล่องက အရမ်းလေးလို့ ငါမ မမော့နိုင်ဘူး။

details.explanation: Remove 'very' and replace with 'so … that' to combine.
details.example: She is very shy. She cannot perform on stage. → She is so shy that she cannot perform on stage.
details.burmese: သူမက အရမ်းရှက်တတ်လို့ ဇာတ်ပွဲမှာ မတင်နိုင်ဘူး။
